ddx.step1_summary:
Key clinical elements:
- Chief complaint: Persistent fever with sweating and feeling unwell for the past 7 days.
- Symptoms: Daily fever; alternating feeling hot and cold, drenching sweats (incl. night sweats); generalized myalgias; nausea with ↓ appetite; mild fluid intake; marked fatigue. No cough, sore throat, ear pain, diarrhea, urinary symptoms, stiff neck, new-onset headache, rash, or joint swelling.
- Onset/duration: Fever began 7 days ago; travel to Vietnam ended 4 weeks ago.
- Aggravating/alleviating: OTC paracetamol/ibuprofen give slight, temporary relief.
- Past medical history: Chronic mechanical back pain; episodic screen-related headaches/migraines.
- Medications: Seroxat (paroxetine); intermittent paracetamol & ibuprofen. 
- Allergies: Pollen (hay fever) only.
- Family history: Father died of myocardial infarction at 68 y.
- Social history: 30-y-old female nurse; up-to-date vaccinations; non-smoker; moderate alcohol; regular exercise. Recent adventurous travel through rural Vietnam with trekking, cycling, river/ farmland exposure; took daily malaria prophylaxis (exact drug unknown, possibly combined).
- Vital signs / exam: None provided (telephone consult).
- Labs/imaging: None yet; physician plans bloods incl. malaria thick/thin films and inflammatory markers.

V: Infective endocarditis: persistent fever and sweats without clear focus; health-care exposure as nurse. Needs exclusion though no murmurs or risk factors mentioned.
I: Malaria: Returned from Vietnam; febrile illness with sweats, myalgias, cyclic hot/cold; prophylaxis not fully protective or may have been non-adherent.
Dengue or other arboviral infection: Rural SE-Asia travel; fever, myalgia, malaise, sweats; incubation can be up to 2 weeks, sometimes longer.
Typhoid/enteric fever: Travel to endemic area; prolonged fever, sweats, GI upset (nausea).
N: Lymphoma (e.g., Hodgkin): B-symptoms of fever, night sweats, fatigue in young adult.
Leukemia: Unexplained fever and sweats could be constitutional symptoms.
D: Tuberculosis (chronic infection/degenerative tissue damage): Night sweats, fever after travel to endemic region.
I2: Drug-induced fever (NSAIDs, SSRI): Persistent fever unresponsive to antipyretics, though rare.
A: Adult-onset Still’s disease / connective-tissue inflammatory condition: Quotidian fevers, myalgia, sweats.
E: Hyperthyroidism: Heat intolerance, sweating, weight changes can mimic fever, though true temperature elevation less common.

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Classic febrile illness with cyclic hot/cold sweats, myalgia, and recent travel to rural Vietnam 4 weeks ago. Prophylaxis is not 100 % protective and adherence/drug unknown.
supporting_evidence: Returned from malaria-endemic country (Vietnam) 4 weeks ago
opposing_evidence: Took daily antimalarial prophylaxis (unknown drug, possible good adherence)
No mention of classical rigors or periodicity

step3_ranked_ddx.diagnosis: Acute systemic viral infection (e.g., influenza, COVID-19 or other viral)
step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Common cause of 1-week fever, myalgias and malaise without focal signs; could coincide with seasonal viruses or COVID-19 despite lack of respiratory symptoms.
supporting_evidence: Fever, myalgias, fatigue and nausea are typical viral systemic symptoms
No localized infectious focus found on review of systems
opposing_evidence: Duration already 7 days with persistent high fever (many simple viral illnesses improve by now)

step3_ranked_ddx.diagnosis: Dengue (or other arboviral such as Chikungunya)
step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Endemic in Vietnam; presents with fever, severe myalgia (‘break-bone’), sweats; mosquito exposure likely. Incubation usually 4-10 days but late presentation can occur.
supporting_evidence: Recent travel to mosquito-endemic rural SE-Asia
opposing_evidence: Onset 3–4 weeks after return (beyond typical incubation)
No rash, retro-orbital pain, or marked arthralgia reported

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Prolonged fever with nonspecific GI symptoms after travel to endemic area; incubation up to ~21 days so possible but less typical.
supporting_evidence: Travel to Vietnam with rural food/water exposure
opposing_evidence: No abdominal pain, diarrhea/constipation, or rose-spot rash
Return travel >3 weeks ago (at upper incubation limit)

step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Night sweats, fever, fatigue are B-symptoms; warrants consideration if infection excluded.
opposing_evidence: Very acute onset (1 week) more typical of infection
No weight loss, lymphadenopathy, or pruritus reported
